skill.name: frontend-components
skill.description: Build reusable, composable UI components with single responsibilities, clear prop interfaces, proper state management, and minimal coupling. Use this skill when creating or editing React components (.tsx, .jsx files), when designing component APIs with props, when implementing component composition patterns, when managing local component state, when building shadcn/ui components, when creating shared UI components in resources/js/Components/, when implementing component documentation, or when refactoring large components into smaller, focused pieces.
skill.summary: Guide AI assistants to build reusable React components with clear props, focused state, and maintainable composition.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: The markdown backtick findings are false positives caused by file extensions and a component directory path in prose. The relative link on line 28 is a confirmed filesystem-boundary issue because it points outside the skill package to unscanned instructions.

remediation.issue: The skill references documentation outside its own package with a traversing relative path.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced component standards inside the skill directory, then link to that local packaged file.

static_findings.snippet: - When creating new React components in `.tsx` or `.jsx` files

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 uses markdown inline code for .tsx and .jsx file extensions. It does not invoke a shell, execute Ruby, or pass user input to a command.

Line 28 instructs the agent to follow a ../../../ relative link outside the skill package. That can pull in unscanned external instructions and crosses the expected filesystem boundary.

content.value_statement: Developers need consistent React components that stay easy to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward focused APIs and composition.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of React components in .tsx and .jsx files.
Encourages clear prop interfaces and TypeScript type definitions.
Supports component composition from smaller focused pieces.
Helps choose local state, reducers, or lifted parent state.
Applies guidance to shadcn/ui customization and shared UI components.
Supports refactoring large components into smaller maintainable units.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not include executable component generators.
It does not define a complete design system or visual style guide.
It depends on project conventions for naming, folder layout, and dependencies.
Its referenced standards file is outside the packaged skill and may be unavailable.

use_cases.title: Create Shared UI Components
use_cases.description: Build buttons, forms, modals, or cards with clear props and limited internal state.

use_cases.title: Refactor Large React Views
use_cases.description: Split a large component into smaller parts with focused responsibilities and cleaner composition.

use_cases.title: Standardize AI Component Work
use_cases.description: Give AI coding tools consistent rules for React props, state boundaries, and reusable UI patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new reusable component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable React component for [purpose]. Use clear props, simple state, and a focused responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Component Props
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to clean an existing component API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component API. Simplify the props, add useful TypeScript types, and explain the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Component Composition
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request to split a large component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this large React component into smaller composable components. Keep behavior the same and explain each new responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Design Shared Component Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for project-wide component standards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a shared component approach for this feature. Include state placement, composition boundaries, naming, and documentation needs.

output_examples.input: Create a reusable confirmation modal for deleting records.
output_examples.output: A focused modal design with explicit open, cancel, confirm, title, and description props. The result separates presentation from deletion behavior.

output_examples.input: Refactor a dashboard widget that mixes fetching, filtering, and rendering.
output_examples.output: A refactoring plan that separates data handling, filter controls, and display components while preserving the current user workflow.

output_examples.input: Document how to use a shared form field component.
output_examples.output: A concise usage guide describing required props, optional labels, validation display, and examples for common form layouts.

best_practices: Keep each component focused on one responsibility and one clear rendering concern.
Use typed props that expose the smallest practical public API.
Document reusable components with expected props, states, and common usage examples.
anti_patterns: Do not place unrelated data fetching, formatting, and layout logic in one component.
Do not expose broad props that leak internal implementation details.
Do not create shared components before repeated use or a stable interface exists.

faq.question: Does this skill generate React components automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides an AI assistant while the assistant edits or creates React component files.

faq.question: Can it work with TypeScript components?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill specifically references .tsx files and TypeScript prop interface design.

faq.question: Does it support shadcn/ui?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for building or customizing shadcn/ui components.

faq.question: Is this a full frontend architecture guide?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on reusable components, props, state placement, and composition.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publication?
faq.answer: The referenced component standards should be bundled inside the skill instead of linked through a traversing path.
